rule: Force benchmark: trap bar (high handle) e1RM 2.0-2.25 x bodyweight.
summary: No normative trap-bar or hex-bar data for trained men were found; the hex-bar studies retrieved report 1RM relationships, not population norms. Powerlifting norms show that relative strength falls with body mass (about 0.015-0.020 x BW per kg in the deadlift), so a linear BW multiplier is a crude target for a 95 kg athlete. Reviews support more strength as broadly beneficial but give no threshold for a hybrid athlete. Keep it as a coach target, labelled as such.

sources.note: Montenegro 2026: percentile norms for drug-tested powerlifters; deadlift multiplier declines 0.015-0.020 per kg of body mass; argues against fixed BW multipliers.
Suchomel 2016 review: greater strength improves jumping, sprinting and change of direction; describes strength deficit/association/reserve phases but no hybrid-athlete number.
Hex-bar 1RM in 23 mixed-training adults relates to isometric pull force; no normative ratios.
